overview: White plays the a-pawn a move, with no central claim; the idea is to gain queenside space and perhaps a rook lift (Ra3) while keeping options open. Black simply occupies the centre with ...e5 or ...d5 and gets a comfortable game. Play usually transposes into a reversed or flank opening.

white_ideas.idea: Ra3 or a5 for queenside space
Transpose into a regular d4, c4 or Nf3 set-up

black_ideas.idea: Develop and punish the wasted tempo

typical_structures.structure: Any reversed or regular set-up; no fixed structure

character.notes: Slow flank move; unforced and roughly equal.

gambit.notes: No pawn offered; 2.Ra3 is a trap not a gambit.

soundness.notes: Not refuted, only a wasted tempo.

approach.notes: Strong players almost never choose it.

level.notes: Few lines and plans are vague; not a good first repertoire.

sublines_that_differ.name: Meadow Hay Trap
sublines_that_differ.how: A joke trap line, not a main line.

character.reason: Slow and unforcing, neither especially solid nor sharp.

soundness.reason: Loses a tempo, not a refutation.

structure.reason: Flank opening with the centre undecided.

level.reason: No theory but no clear plan either.

plans.reason: No well-defined plan from the flank pawn.
